japan-1905:p0153_2.rationale: Annual salt-field area, furnaces and salt output are accompanied by production value and average price per koku.

japan-1906:p0545_4.rationale: Year rows report male and female opium smokers, totals and smokers per hundred population; licensing and treatment are not identified.

japan-1907:p0625_1.rationale: Army divisions report war deaths from wounds, disease and accidents, and total deaths.

japan-1908-09:p0045_1.rationale: The 1907 flood losses include deaths, injuries, destroyed houses and infrastructure, damaged farms/crops and yen loss totals.

japan-1910:p0347_2.rationale: Annual figures count licensed patent medicines and receipts from 1902 through 1906. The licensed medical preparations are the subject; the word patent does not make this an inventions or trademark-registration table.

japan-1910:p0690_1.rationale: The roster names successive Formosa governors-general and their appointment and relief dates, with no statistical quantities.

japan-1911:p0638_2.rationale: The only commodity rows are pan-fired and basket-fired green tea, compared by export value over four years.

japan-1912:p0483_6.rationale: Conscription insurance is measured through company count, capital, premium reserve, claims paid and insured contracts/policies.

japan-1913:p0065_1.rationale: Annual passport issues to Japanese going abroad are split by sex and explicitly presented as evidence of emigration trends.

japan-1914:p0358_3.rationale: Male, female and child operatives at army cloth works have measured work hours, rest periods, holidays and annual working days.

japan-1915:p0570_1.rationale: Army training schools report staff, students, graduates and admissions across military specialisms.

japan-1916:p0770_6.rationale: Import values cover six principal commodity groups over three years; opium is one part of the multi-product summary.

japan-1917:p0779_6.rationale: The table compares annual import values across opium, rice, petroleum, tobacco, oilcakes and timber.

japan-1918:p0353_1.rationale: Government workplace mutual relief societies are compared by membership, beneficiaries and pooled payments for wounded and deceased members, medical expenses and other aid.

japan-1919-20:p0816_2.rationale: Raids attributed by the source to aborigines are measured by police and civilian killed and wounded; Indigenous people and police casualties are explicit, while a particular control policy is not stated.

japan-1920-21:p0338_2.rationale: The two year rows count visitors to imperial and educational museums and to the zoological garden.

japan-1920-21:p0456_1.rationale: The three numbered textual provisions identify food/drink, medicines/compounding methods and harmful articles as not patentable. Numbers enumerate exclusions from patent protection rather than quantities.

japan-1920-21:p0720_3.rationale: The Tokyo electric tramway series gives mileage, daily passengers and daily passenger receipts for 1917–1919. Revenue is an operating measure of the identified urban tram system.

japan-1923:p0105_2.rationale: Each dated earthquake or earthquake-associated tidal wave has destroyed-house, death and injury quantities.

japan-1923:p0453_1.rationale: The Tokyo theatre row gives substantive totals of days open and tickets sold.

japan-1924-25:p0963_2.rationale: Chinese, British and other foreign residents are compared before the earthquake and in June 1924 using both family and population counts.

japan-1930:p0513_2.rationale: The 1925–1928 series tabulates receipts, payments and their balance specifically for invisible trade in thousands of yen. It does not present merchandise plus capital/current accounts sufficient to classify the whole table as balance of payments.

japan-1930:p0559_1.rationale: The rows count residents of Kwantung Province, the railway zone and consular jurisdiction by Japanese, Korean, Chinese and other nationality categories; no administrative powers are tabulated.

japan-1935:p0308_1.rationale: Ministry and programme rows allocate multiyear public appropriations for relief and restoration after the 1934 disasters, including infrastructure and school rebuilding.

japan-1937:p0409_1.rationale: The two complete parts combine monthly wholesale prices, exports, imports, industrial production, railway freight, bank clearings, note issue and stock quotations. This is a broad economic indicator set; choosing three individual components would misrepresent its scope.

japan-1939-40:p0696_1.rationale: All expenditure rows fund educational administration, schooling, social education, special education, universities or libraries, with a total in yen. This is a budget devoted to education rather than a general budget with one school row.

japan-1939-40:p1088_1.rationale: Ordinary and extraordinary revenue and expenditure, with totals for the 1936–37 Kwantung budget, organise every numerical row. The leased-territory designation identifies whose accounts these are; no governing relationship or colonial powers are tabulated.

japan-1939-40:p1093_2.rationale: The body lists foreign concessions and international settlements with creation dates and measured areas, then explicitly identifies French, Portuguese and British leased territories.

japan-1942-43:p1068_6.rationale: The supplied row identifies the French concession at Tientsin, its creation date and an area of about 2,360 se. The concession is the substantive foreign-privilege subject; its measured area makes this a statistical mixed record.

japan-1942-43:p1069_1.rationale: Foreign concession and international settlement rows give creation dates and substantive territorial areas in se.

japan-1942-43:p1157_1.rationale: The complete emperor roster (reigns 54–124) pairs monarchs, era names and calendar date ranges. Its Duration of Reign column contains accession/end years rather than measured reign lengths; dates and reign numbers are reference designations.

japan-1946-48:p0285_1.rationale: Monthly Reconstruction Finance Bank lending is measured by recipient industry in million yen.

manchuria-1929:p0188_1.rationale: Annual salt production is counted separately for Japanese and Chinese producers and in total; leased-territory context does not itself establish a colonial-rule subject.

manchuria-1931:p0022_3.rationale: Annual engagements and dead/wounded losses of Japanese Army railway guards and Japanese police are expressly attributed to attacks described by the source as bandit attacks.

manchuria-1936:p0096_1.rationale: Japanese kindergartens, primary, middle, girls’ high and miscellaneous schools in the leased territory and railway zone are counted with pupils and teachers; the explicit subject is Japanese education overseas.

manchuria-1939:p0091_1.rationale: All 23 self-protective villages are grouped into dated settlement cohorts, with household/member counts and cultivated hectares. These support migration, household demographics and cultivated land. No nationality, sponsoring foreign state or explicit relation to colonial expansion appears in the complete record, so the narrower settler-migration tag and either imperial topic lack sufficient evidence.

manchuria-year-book-1931:p0041_1.rationale: Dated event descriptions span dynastic succession, exploration, treaties, railways, wars and political changes; dates and an incidental troop number remain narrative chronology.

manchuria-year-book-1931:p0216_1.rationale: The annual series compares wholesale commodity-price indices across Dairen, Tokyo, London, New York and China, with a silver quotation index and explicit source notes.

manchuria-year-book-1932-33:p0531_1.rationale: The resident population is classified jointly by occupation, Japanese/Chinese/Korean/other nationality and male/female sex, with totals and percentages; no employment-status measures establish a labour table.

manchoukuo-1934:p0497_1.rationale: Machinery and tool enterprises report factory counts, capital and output values by city and Japanese or Manchurian ownership categories.

manchukuo-directory-1938:p0039_2.rationale: Central and local official counts are cross-tabulated by four civil-service appointment ranks, with quantitative subtotals and totals.

japan-manchoukuo-1934:p1-0367_1.rationale: The complete business barometer combines several wholesale and retail price indices with actual earnings, wage rates and employment. Economic-indicators covers the full set, with labour a substantial organised component.

japan-manchoukuo-1934:p1-0495_2.rationale: The two-page roster identifies commercial and staple-products museums by name, location and establishment year; its year column records dates rather than quantitative observations.

japan-manchoukuo-1934:p2-0003_2.rationale: Five meteorological observatories are identified with latitude, longitude, elevation in metres and establishment year. The inventory concerns facilities supporting scientific observation. There are no atmospheric-condition readings to support weather, and the leased-territory wording does not make colonial governing powers a subject.

japan-manchoukuo-1936:p1-0264_3.rationale: Annual subscriber counts distinguish individual, party and extension subscriptions and quantify pending connection applications.

japan-manchoukuo-1936:p1-0365_1.rationale: The two parts give town/village revenue, including several tax categories, and public expenditure by service, distinguishing settled and budget accounts.

japan-manchoukuo-1936:p1-0407_4.rationale: Automobile insurers are measured by company counts, insured policy values, reserves, premiums, claims and business expenses over five years.

japan-manchoukuo-1938:p1-0066_4.rationale: Observatory rows compare precipitation in selected months, annual totals and maximum daily rainfall in millimetres.

japan-manchoukuo-1938:p1-0383_1.rationale: Insurers and annual totals are compared by contract numbers/amounts, premiums, interest, claims, business expenses and reserves.

japan-manchoukuo-1938:p1-0965_1.rationale: For ten narcotic stations and annual totals, the columns measure capacity, admissions, persons reported cured, cure ratios and treatment days, separately for opium and other narcotic patients. Treatment outcomes and the substantial opium breakdown support these labels.

japan-manchoukuo-1939:p1-0258_2.rationale: Every national/city column is a cost-of-living index for 1929 and 1932–1937; footnotes identify the Japanese compilers and a separate 1914 base for thirteen cities. This is the specific living-cost series rather than a general multi-domain economic barometer.

japan-manchoukuo-1939:p1-0283_3.rationale: Part (a) reports tonnages of multiple commodities handled by state railways; part (b) reports freight and passenger distances and receipts per ton, passenger or kilometre.

japan-manchoukuo-1939:p1-0329_1.rationale: Both parts track outstanding debentures, first by issuing bank and then across industrial company sectors; they are corporate borrowing rather than public debt.

japan-manchoukuo-1939:p1-0591_1.rationale: Both parts count head-office companies and outside companies branch offices by business sector and year.

japan-manchoukuo-1939:p1-0935_1.rationale: Chinese labourer arrivals in Manchuria are counted annually and monthly by agricultural, mining, manufacturing, transport and other callings; no state-sponsored settlement scheme is stated.

japan-manchoukuo-1940:p0034_1.rationale: Annual and monthly business indicators combine wholesale and retail prices, living costs, labour earnings, wage rates, employment and industrial production. The aggregate tag represents the complete multi-domain barometer; labour is also a substantial organised component.

japan-manchoukuo-1940:p0115_6.rationale: The provincial rows count people described by the source as bandits surrendering in 1935, with a total of 6,713. The table reports that category and surrender outcome; it does not identify political aims or military forces involved.

nanyo-tokei-1937:p0032_1.rationale: Three bands count administrative correspondence by the Governor’s Secretariat, departments, branches and public agencies. Notes explicitly trace departmental reorganizations and where predecessor offices’ documents are included.

nanyo-tokei-1937:p0033_2.rationale: Known and cleared crime cases are counted for many Criminal Code and special-law offences by year and branch office.

nanyo-tokei-1937:p0034_1.rationale: Arrested persons are counted by offence, Japanese or islander category, year and branch, with foreigners identified in parentheses.

nanyo-tokei-1937:p0041_3.rationale: Both parts count 狩獵免狀 licences by year and branch office, dividing 遊獵, 職獵 and 學術研究其ノ他. This is hunting licensing administration spanning recreation, professional activity and research. The foreign-licence annotations and note that islanders have no applicable entries are incidental, not an Indigenous-peoples subject.

nanyo-tokei-1937:p0049_1.rationale: Year and branch parts count persons summarily sentenced by offence, pairing Japanese and islander columns and identifying foreigners in parentheses. Specific regulatory offences remain categories of the overall justice table.

nanyo-tokei-1937:p0077_2.rationale: Company counts, nominal capital, paid-up capital and corporate forms are tabulated by business sector, including a separate local-head-office subset.

nanyo-tokei-1937:p0079_3.rationale: Fishing boats are counted by engine and tonnage class, alongside crew numbers and catch values by year and branch office.

nanyo-tokei-1932:p0068_1.rationale: Three complete bands count administrative documents received and dispatched by the Governor’s office, departments, branches, courts and other Nanyo government agencies. This measures colonial governing machinery, including its administrative correspondence, rather than public postal traffic.

nanyo-tokei-1932:p0114_1.rationale: Across the total and six branch blocks, passport recipients are counted by occupation and Japanese or islander category, further divided by sex.

nanyo-tokei-1932:p0143_1.rationale: Second-instance convictions are counted by Criminal Code and special-law offence, year, and Japanese or islander category.

nanyo-tokei-1932:p0152_1.rationale: District court procurators offices report criminal cases prosecuted by offence category across years and office branches.

nanyo-tokei-1932:p0155_1.rationale: High Court prosecutions count persons by offence and year separately for Japanese and islanders.

nanyo-tokei-1932:p0213_1.rationale: Both bands count recipients and grants for cane planting, clearance, nurseries, seedlings, green manure, sugar shipment and factories, with Japanese/islander breakdowns. The subject is support for the sugar industry rather than a general public budget.

nanyo-tokei-1932:p0269_1.rationale: The totals and all six branch blocks count popular-education associations and members, including youth, women’s, education and alumni groups; membership is systematically split by sex and Japanese/islander categories.

japan-tokei-1935:p0033_1.rationale: The commerce, banking, finance and trade summary combines companies and capital, currency, bank deposits and loans, clearing, postal finance, insurance, prices and merchandise trade. Economic-indicators represents the complete summary rather than three selected financial components.

japan-tokei-1935:p0092_3.rationale: This is not a fourth opium-business-licensing inventory. One full part measures sugar and molasses output; the other measures raw-opium stocks, licensed smokers by source population/sex and prepared-opium sales. Both substantial subjects justify its distinct manufacturing/narcotics assignment.

japan-tokei-1935:p0169_2.rationale: All three parts compare admission applicants, entrants and admission percentages across middle/girls schools, universities and numerous specialist/professional school fields.

japan-tokei-1935:p0182_1.rationale: Year and locality parts count crimes cleared by police across criminal-code and special-law offences; territorial comparisons do not establish a colonial-administration subject.

japan-tokei-1935:p0230_1.rationale: Town and village expenditures, including special accounts, are divided among many public services by year and prefecture; education and sanitation are items within general accounts.

japan-tokei-1935:p0240_1.rationale: Military police personnel are counted annually across officer and enlisted ranks and civilian employee categories.

japan-tokei-1935:p0245_2.rationale: Year and locality rows count naval recruits by seamen, telegraph, aviation, engine-room, band, medical and paymaster branches.

japan-tokei-1938:p0142_1.rationale: All year and locality rows enumerate social-work facilities across coordination/research, child protection, housing and other economic protection, employment relief, poor relief, medical protection and judicial aftercare. The aggregate welfare-institutions tag describes the full multi-function inventory, including the colonial rows, without elevating incidental facility types to separate subjects.

japan-tokei-1938:p0150_3.rationale: Seamen book holders are counted by detailed age bands at year end; these are an occupational group, not general residents.

japan-tokei-1938:p0153_1.rationale: All three parts are wage-index series, distinguishing manufacturing branches, transport/communications workers and mining branches rather than output in those industries.

japan-tokei-1938:p0154_2.rationale: Government enterprise worker mutual-aid associations report membership, contributions and investment income, benefit recipients and benefit payments across illness, retirement and survivor support.

japan-tokei-1938:p0170_1.rationale: Six parts compare applicants, admitted students and admission rates across middle/girls schools, universities and specialist/technical fields in Japan proper.

japan-tokei-1938:p0179_4.rationale: Police stations and posts, officers by rank and population per patrolman are counted by year and territory; ordinary police provision is the subject.

japan-tokei-1940:p0087_3.rationale: Both body blocks give annual wage indices across factory, transport/communications and mine-worker branches, with an explicit change of index base in the note.

japan-tokei-1940:p0100_2.rationale: Year, prefecture and territory rows count police stations/posts and personnel by police rank, with population per constable as a staffing ratio.

japan-tokei-1940:p0134_1.rationale: All three parts report outstanding local borrowing, broken down by borrowing public bodies, purpose and prefecture; these are debt balances rather than budget expenditure flows.

manchoukuo-1942:IMG_5455_1.rationale: Each 1912–1944 row equates Christian years with Japanese foundation/era years, Manchoukuo eras and Chinese Republican years. The figures are calendar designations, with no substantive statistical measurements.

manchoukuo-1942:IMG_5508_1.rationale: The complete 1616–1941 year/event sequence covers successive rulers, wars, diplomacy, railways, government, settlement and industry. Dates and occasional quantities within event descriptions serve a general historical chronology, rather than a quantitative series.

manchoukuo-1942:IMG_5879_1.rationale: The complete two-page list supplies prison names and locations under the Prison Law, with no capacities, inmates or other substantive quantities.
